readingInstruction: Read Psalm 139:13-24. You may have read the first half before. Read this section on God’s formation of us in the womb and the prayer to be searched and led. Notice how awe and honest self-examination fit together.
settingTheScene: Psalm 139 is one of the most intimate psalms, celebrating God’s knowledge, presence, and creative care. The first twelve verses describe how God knows us completely and is present everywhere. Verses 13 to 18 describe how God made us. Verses 19 to 22 are an outburst against the wicked. Verses 23 and 24 are a closing prayer for God to search the speaker’s own heart. It connects with the Prison Epistles’ emphasis that we are God’s workmanship, known and led by him.
observation: “For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother’s womb” (v. 13).
“I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made” (v. 14).
“My frame was not hidden from you, when I was being made in secret” (v. 15).
“In your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them” (v. 16).
“How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them!” (v. 17).
“If I would count them, they are more than the sand” (v. 18).
“Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!” (v. 23).
“And lead me in the way everlasting!” (v. 24).
interpretation:
David marvels at his own creation. “For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother’s womb.” God is a weaver and an artist. “I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well.” The human being is a marvel of design, and knowing this produces praise. This psalm is often cited for the dignity of life before birth. The Bible regards the unborn as persons known and formed by God. Every human life is intentionally made.

“My frame was not hidden from you, when I was being made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth.” The “depths of the earth” is a poetic image for the womb, an echo of Adam’s formation from the earth. “Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them.” God’s knowledge extends to our days before we have lived them. This is not a statement of fatalism but of providence. Every day belongs to God.

The reaction: “How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them! If I would count them, they are more than the sand. I awake, and I am still with you.” Dazed by God’s greatness, David finds himself still in God’s presence. Verses 19 to 22 give a strong expression of hatred of God’s enemies: “Do you not hate those who hate you, O LORD?” This sounds jarring, but David’s motive is zeal for God, not private spite. Christians read this in light of Jesus’ command to love our enemies. We hate sin and pray for sinners.

Then the psalm turns from the enemies to himself. “Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts! And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting!” After praising God’s knowledge of him, David invites that knowledge to examine him. He does not fear being exposed because he trusts the one who exposes. He wants to be corrected. “The way everlasting” is the way that leads to life, the path of faithfulness. This is a good prayer for each morning.

In Christ, this prayer is safe. Christ knows our sins and yet bore them. He is the way everlasting (John 14:6). The one who searches us is the one who loves us.
connection: Jeremiah 1:5 says God knew the prophet before forming him in the womb. Job 10:8-12 and Psalm 119:73 also speak of God’s making. Ecclesiastes 11:5 compares the mystery of the womb to God’s works. Luke 1:39-45 mentions John leaping in the womb. Psalm 51:6 and Hebrews 4:12-13 speak of God’s searching knowledge. Psalm 19:12-14 prays for cleansing from hidden faults. Romans 8:29 and Ephesians 1:4 speak of God’s knowledge before creation. John 14:6 says Jesus is the way. Matthew 5:43-48 teaches love of enemies.
application:
Thank God today for how you were made. Name something about yourself you’ve struggled to accept.

Pray verses 23 and 24 at the start of the day, and be ready for the answer.

Treat every person you meet as someone fearfully and wonderfully made, including the unborn and the elderly.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that you are fearfully and wonderfully made.
Ask him to search your heart and lead you in the everlasting way.
Tell him what anxious thoughts you want him to know.
